ask: 'You were right to bring him straight in.' / 'How long after breakfast did the rash come up?' / 'Whereabouts on his face — near the eyes, or the lips?' / 'I'm going to run through a short list of specific things. Just yes or no.' / 'Before I settle on the food — any new medicine, any sting, ANYTHING NEW ON HIS SKIN?'

'Those observations are normal for a five-year-old.' / 'Ryan has had a MILD allergic reaction.' / 'I was deliberately looking for the signs of a severe reaction, AND HE HAS NONE OF THEM.' / 'That is exactly why I want to keep him and watch him, rather than send him home.'

'Adrenaline pens are for children who have had a severe reaction, or who THE SPECIALIST decides are at high risk.' / 'If I gave one to every mild reaction, IT WOULD STOP MEANING ANYTHING.' / 'Tell us immediately if his tongue swells, his voice changes, his breathing gets noisy, he drools, or he goes floppy.' / 'I'll give you an ALLERGY ACTION PLAN.' / 'Cake can contain egg, milk, wheat and nut at the same time.' / 'I can't promise it will never happen again, but I can tell you exactly what to do if it does.'

VARIANT — THE BEE STING: ask where he was stung, IS THE STING STILL IN THE SKIN, has he been stung before and what happened, and HAS HE VOMITED OR HAD TUMMY PAIN SINCE. 'I can see the sting is still there. I'm going to FLICK IT OUT SIDEWAYS RATHER THAN SQUEEZE IT, because squeezing pushes more venom in.' THE CATCH: FOR INSECT VENOM, PERSISTENT ABDOMINAL PAIN OR VOMITING COUNTS AS ANAPHYLAXIS — WHICH IT DOES NOT FOR FOOD. Repeated vomiting with cramping pain after a sting IS adrenaline, even with no airway sign; and confirmed sting anaphylaxis earns referral for VENOM IMMUNOTHERAPY, which is genuinely disease-modifying. / VARIANT — THE WHEEZING ASTHMATIC: THE LABEL FLIPS, AND SAY IT FAST: 'Ryan is wheezing after eating something new. I CANNOT SAFELY SEPARATE AN ASTHMA ATTACK FROM A SEVERE ALLERGIC REACTION HERE, SO I AM TREATING IT AS THE SEVERE ALLERGIC REACTION. Adrenaline first, intramuscular, outer thigh — then salbutamol, then oxygen.' If challenged: 'because DELAY TO ADRENALINE is the recognised contributor to death in food anaphylaxis, and adrenaline treats bronchospasm as well. If I'm wrong, I've given adrenaline to a child having an asthma attack, WHICH IS SAFE. If I withhold it and I'm wrong, HE CAN DIE.'

VARIANT — 'IT HAPPENED BEFORE', volunteered late: 'thank you — THAT CHANGES WHAT I DO NEXT, THOUGH NOT WHAT I DO TODAY. Today is still a mild reaction and today's treatment is the same. BUT A SECOND REACTION TO THE SAME FOOD MAKES THE ALLERGY FAR MORE CERTAIN, and it moves him up the list for the allergy clinic. I'll mark the referral URGENT and ask them specifically to do A RISK ASSESSMENT FOR AN ADRENALINE PEN.' (This version punishes candidates who stopped taking a history the moment they had a diagnosis.) / THE DETERIORATION VERSION: 'THIS HAS CHANGED — I'M STOPPING AND TREATING THIS AS A SEVERE ALLERGIC REACTION NOW.' Lay him flat, IM ADRENALINE 0.01 mg/kg of 1:1000 into the OUTER MID-THIGH, call for help, high-flow oxygen, repeat at five minutes, IV access, 20 mL/kg if hypotensive, OBSERVE AT LEAST FOUR HOURS AFTER THE LAST DOSE. IN THIS VERSION, AND ONLY THIS VERSION, YOU SAY THE WORD.
pefe: Role-player: James, 38, diesel mechanic, father of Ryan, 5; his wife is at work and does not know yet. He drove Ryan straight to ED twenty minutes after the rash appeared. REGISTER: FRIGHTENED BUT CONTROLLED — not hostile, does not cry. HE INTERRUPTS ONCE, EARLY, WITH 'IS IT SERIOUS?' — if the doctor promises an answer in a couple of minutes, he settles; IF THEY GIVE A DIAGNOSIS BEFORE EXAMINING, HE PRESSES: 'HOW CAN YOU KNOW ALREADY?' HIDDEN AGENDA: a boy at Ryan's school carries an EpiPen and he wants one — DO NOT RAISE IT until the diagnosis has been explained; if the doctor never invites questions, ASK AT ABOUT SEVEN MINUTES: 'SHOULDN'T HE HAVE ONE OF THOSE EPIPENS?'

THE ANSWERS: breakfast about half an hour ago, rash fifteen to twenty minutes later, started on the cheeks and now on the chest, RAISED AND BUMPY, VERY ITCHY; LIPS NORMAL; no drooling, no noisy breathing, no shortness of breath, VOICE THE SAME, no vomiting, COMPLETELY WITH IT — he has been running around the waiting room. TOAST WITH PEANUT BUTTER, AND IF ASKED, THE FIRST TIME HE HAS HAD IT. No medicines, no stings. THE NEW SUNSCREEN ON HIS FACE AND CHEST THIS MORNING IS VOLUNTEERED ONLY IF ASKED ABOUT CREAMS OR ANYTHING NEW ON THE SKIN. Never happened before. No family food allergy; mother has hay fever, sister has asthma, Ryan had bronchiolitis as a baby; otherwise well, no medicines, immunisations up to date, behaving normally.

HOW TO PLAY IT: ANSWER ONLY WHAT IS ASKED. DO NOT OFFER the sunscreen, the first-time peanut butter, or the family history unprompted. IF THE DOCTOR ASKS 'ANY OTHER SYMPTOMS?' AS ONE VAGUE QUESTION, ANSWER 'NO' — MAKE THEM ASK THE SIX RED FLAGS INDIVIDUALLY. If they ask about the rash as 'on his face?', answer 'yes, his face' AND WAIT — only if they ask WHERE on the face do you say cheeks, not lips. IF THEY SAY THE WORD ANAPHYLAXIS TO YOU, LOOK ALARMED: 'IS THAT THE ONE THAT KILLS PEOPLE?' If they promise he will be completely fine, ask 'CAN YOU GUARANTEE THAT?' Close by asking 'SO WHAT DO I DO IF IT HAPPENS AGAIN?' Mark out of 10: introduction and fear acknowledged in fifteen seconds; interval established; asked WHERE on the face; ALL SIX RED FLAGS; medicines, stings and skin products with the SUNSCREEN FOUND; ASKED FOR OXYGEN SATURATION; said the observations were normal FOR AGE; ONE severity label justified with named negatives; THE PEN REFUSED WITH A REASON AND A PATHWAY; specific red flags given and the ALLERGY ACTION PLAN named.
Lips and tongue — No swelling
Voice — No hoarseness
What you must ask for — SATURATIONS — forgetting them and trying to add it after the examiner has moved on is the classic miss
The deterioration version — The father reports THE VOICE HAS GONE CROAKY in the last few minutes, or the card says STRIDOR — stop the history and treat it as severe
fails: ★ Saying the word ANAPHYLAXIS as part of the diagnosis, or hedging between two labels — 'it's an allergic reaction, though it might be anaphylaxis' is the single commonest fail
★ Giving, or offering to prescribe, adrenaline to a stable child with skin-only signs — and handing over a pen to stop the father worrying
Discharging him from the cubicle with no observation period, or promising he will be completely fine
Asking three of the six red flags and moving on, or asking 'any other symptoms?' as one vague question, which the father answers 'no'

Accepting 'on his face' and never establishing that the lips were spared; deciding it was the food before asking about the sunscreen; forgetting to ask for saturations; and announcing shock because the blood pressure was not 120/80
numbers: IM ADRENALINE 0.01 mg/kg of 1:1000, MAX 0.5 mg, OUTER MID-THIGH · repeat at 5 minutes if no improvement · AUTOINJECTOR 150 microgram for 7.5-20 kg, 300 microgram above 20 kg · OBSERVE AT LEAST 4 HOURS after the last adrenaline dose · onset usually within 30 minutes, up to 2 hours

Fluid bolus 20 mL/kg normal saline if hypotensive · cetirizine 5 mg daily for 2-5 years, or loratadine 5 mg VERIFY · weight (age + 4) x 2, so a 5-year-old is about 18 kg · TWO PENS AND TWO PLANS, home and school · ABOUT 1 IN 5 ANAPHYLAXIS PRESENTATIONS HAS NO SKIN SIGN · FOR INSECT VENOM, vomiting or abdominal pain COUNTS as anaphylaxis; for food it does not · MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33

setting: HISTORY AND EXPLANATION — general practice, BOTH PARENTS PRESENT. THERE ARE TWO COMPLAINTS AND YOU MUST NAME BOTH BACK before asking anything: the aggression at school, AND the speech. THE STATION IS MARKED ON LOGICALLY EXCLUDING THE OTHER EXPLANATIONS BEFORE YOU CONCLUDE — A PREMATURE CONCLUSION FAILS EVEN IF IT IS THE RIGHT ONE, which is the handbook's own standard. So ask the ADHD components EVEN WHEN THE ANSWERS ALREADY SAY AUTISM. And never say 'he has autism': say THERE IS A POSSIBILITY, then say that NOBODY SHOULD USE THAT WORD UNTIL A PROPER ASSESSMENT HAS BEEN DONE.
stem: VERSION A (the recall since about 2020): general practice. An 8-YEAR-OLD BOY brought by BOTH PARENTS after AN EPISODE OF AGGRESSIVE BEHAVIOUR AT SCHOOL — and the parents are ALSO WORRIED ABOUT HIS SPEECH. Physical examination card: DEVELOPMENTAL MILESTONES ACHIEVED, GROWTH CHART NORMAL, NO DYSMORPHIC FEATURES. History 6 minutes, then diagnosis and differentials 2 minutes.

VERSION B (the AMC handbook case — never a recall, but the template): the same age, DISRUPTIVE AND LOUD BEHAVIOUR IN CLASS, and the teacher asked the parents to see a doctor. VERSION C (threatened): the same stem WITH SNORING in the findings, which makes it obstructive sleep apnoea.
tasks: Take a history from the parents (6 minutes)
Explain your diagnosis and your differential diagnoses to the parents (2 minutes)
time: OPEN, NAME BOTH COMPLAINTS BACK, AND ADDRESS THE CONCERN · 'I understand how worrying that call from the school must have been' · THE EVENT: exactly what happened, IS THIS THE FIRST TIME, how are things at school generally, BULLYING OR STRESS, any drop in school performance · HOME, AND THIS IS THE KEY PAIR OF SETTINGS: ANY SIMILAR BEHAVIOUR AT HOME, how are things at home generally, HIS RELATIONSHIP WITH BOTH OF YOU AND WITH HIS SIBLING, and FAMILY HISTORY INCLUDING YOURSELVES AS CHILDREN · SPEECH: full sentences, REPETITIVE WORDS OR ECHOING, understands instructions, HAS HE EVER LOST WORDS · THE ASD BLOCK: EYE CONTACT, EMOTION AND EMPATHY · DOES HE LIKE CUDDLES AND HUGS, interest in making friends, OBSESSION WITH AN OBJECT OR TOY, INSISTENCE ON ROUTINES, UPSET BY CHANGE · THEN THE ADHD BLOCK IN THREE COMPONENTS EVEN THOUGH THE ANSWERS ALREADY SAY AUTISM: HYPERACTIVE AND HARD TO SLOW DOWN AND CAN HE WAIT HIS TURN; INATTENTIVE · does he finish homework and remember instructions; IMPULSIVE · does he act without thinking · ODD: anger outbursts and refusal to follow instructions · THEN DEVELOPMENT, VISION AND HEARING, SLEEP AND SNORING, HEAD INJURY, STARING SPELLS OR SEIZURES, MOOD, and BINDS · SUMMARISE, then the possibility WITH A LAY DEFINITION, the reasons drawn from their own words, DIFFERENTIALS EACH WITH A REASON, and the multidisciplinary pathway.
findings: Developmental milestones achieved — growth chart normal — no dysmorphic features

back.dx: A POSSIBILITY OF AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER — never a flat diagnosis. DEFINE IT IN LAY WORDS: 'a DEVELOPMENTAL CONDITION that affects HOW A PERSON PROCESSES INFORMATION, BEHAVES AND SEES THE WORLD. It shows up as DIFFICULTY WITH SOCIAL INTERACTION, DIFFICULTY WITH COMMUNICATION, AND REPETITIVE BEHAVIOURS — AND IT IS A SPECTRUM, so it looks different in every child.' THE REASONS, DRAWN FROM THEIR OWN WORDS: he avoids eye contact and cuddles and prefers to be alone — THE SOCIAL PART; his speech is limited to what he can say and he repeats words — COMMUNICATION; he plays only with the curtain and is very distressed by change — REPETITIVE BEHAVIOURS; AND IT IS HAPPENING BOTH AT SCHOOL AND AT HOME. THE DIFFERENTIALS, EACH WITH A REASON: ADHD — he is NOT hyperactive or impulsive and CAN concentrate on things he likes; OPPOSITIONAL DEFIANT DISORDER — his outbursts come WITH CHANGE, not with defiance; SLEEP APNOEA — he does not snore; HEARING OR VISION PROBLEMS, WHICH CAN CAUSE EXACTLY THIS, and although the school checks were normal you want A FORMAL HEARING TEST; head injury, seizures and thyroid problems — nothing in the history; and LOW MOOD, ANXIETY OR STRESS AT SCHOOL OR HOME — he is frustrated rather than sad, and home is settled. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: 'NOBODY SHOULD USE THE WORD AUTISM UNTIL A PROPER ASSESSMENT HAS BEEN DONE — that means a CHILDREN'S SPECIALIST AND A TEAM INCLUDING A PSYCHOLOGIST AND A SPEECH PATHOLOGIST, who will see him MORE THAN ONCE AND IN MORE THAN ONE SETTING, and gather information from his school.' Arrange the referral AND A HEARING TEST TODAY, connect them with SPEECH THERAPY, SCHOOL LEARNING SUPPORT AND A PARENT SUPPORT SERVICE, and review in a few weeks. AND 'IS IT OUR FAULT?' GETS ONE SENTENCE, NOT A LECTURE ON CAUSES: 'NO — IT IS NOT CAUSED BY ANYTHING YOU HAVE DONE.' VERSION B — A POSSIBILITY OF ADHD: 'a condition of brain development that affects a child's ability to CONCENTRATE, TO SIT STILL, AND TO STOP AND THINK BEFORE ACTING.' Reasons: it happens at school AND at home, he cannot wait his turn or finish tasks, he acts without thinking, AND IT OFTEN RUNS IN FAMILIES. Excluded: autism — he makes friends, talks well and has no rituals; ODD — he is restless rather than defiant; sleep apnoea — no snoring; hearing, vision, seizures, head injury and stress — nothing found. Diagnosis needs A PAEDIATRICIAN WITH RATING SCALES FROM BOTH THE PARENTS AND THE TEACHER; treatment is behavioural strategies and school support, and MEDICATION IS A SPECIALIST DECISION AFTER DIAGNOSIS.
plan: OPEN AND NAME BOTH COMPLAINTS BACK: 'you've both come in with Ethan today — how can I help?' → 'the teacher asked us to see a doctor — he was aggressive at school. AND WE'VE BEEN WORRIED ABOUT HIS SPEECH for a while.' → 'SO THERE ARE TWO THINGS: what happened at school, AND HIS SPEECH. I understand how worrying that call from the school must have been. Is it all right if I ask some questions to understand him properly? We'll make a plan together.' (Choosing one complaint and forgetting the other is the first trap.)

THE EVENT AND SCHOOL: 'can you describe exactly what happened? IS THIS THE FIRST TIME, or have there been other episodes? Overall, how are things at school? ANY BULLYING OR STRESS at school that you know of? Any drop in his school performance?' → he slapped a boy who took his seat, a couple of smaller incidents before, behind in reading and writing, no known bullying.

HOME AND FAMILY — TWO SETTINGS, WHICH IS WHAT THE DIAGNOSIS RESTS ON: 'ANY SIMILAR BEHAVIOUR AT HOME? How are things at home generally? HOW IS HIS RELATIONSHIP WITH YOU BOTH, AND WITH HIS SISTER? Is there anyone in the family with similar behaviour or problems — siblings, parents, OR YOURSELVES AS CHILDREN?' → yes at home too, close family, not close to his sister, nobody in the family. (Accepting 'fine at home' and moving on is the trap — ASK THE RELATIONSHIP QUESTION REGARDLESS, because it is where abuse and stress surface.)

SPEECH: 'tell me about your concern with his speech. Can he talk in FULL SENTENCES? Does he use REPETITIVE WORDS, or repeat things back? Does he UNDERSTAND INSTRUCTIONS? HAS HE EVER LOST WORDS HE USED TO HAVE?' → he can talk but cannot tell you what he wants, repeats the same words and phrases, understands if kept simple, never gone backwards.

THE ASD BLOCK, PREFACED SO IT DOESN'T SOUND ODD — 'some of my next questions may sound unrelated; THEY HELP ME RULE THINGS OUT': 'does he KEEP EYE CONTACT? Does he show emotion and empathy — DOES HE LIKE CUDDLES AND HUGS? Is he interested in MAKING FRIENDS? Is he OBSESSED WITH ANY OBJECT OR TOY? Does he INSIST ON ROUTINES? Does he GET UPSET BY ANY CHANGE in his routine or surroundings?' → looks past you, hates cuddles, prefers his own company, THE CURTAIN FOR HOURS, screams if furniture is moved.

THE ADHD BLOCK IN THREE COMPONENTS — ASK IT ANYWAY: 'is he VERY ENERGETIC AND DIFFICULT TO SLOW DOWN? CAN HE WAIT IN A LINE OR WAIT HIS TURN? Any trouble concentrating — DOES HE FINISH HIS HOMEWORK? Does he REMEMBER INSTRUCTIONS? DOES HE ACT WITHOUT THINKING?' → no, he sits for hours; finishes homework if he likes it; not impulsive. THEN ODD: 'any ANGER OUTBURSTS or temper tantrums? Does he REFUSE TO FOLLOW INSTRUCTIONS?' → he does not accept no, but it is that he CANNOT COPE, not defiance. (Skipping ADHD because the answers already say autism is the named trap — the component questions ARE the marks.)

DEVELOPMENT, SENSES, SLEEP, ORGANIC, MOOD AND BINDS: development and growth; VISION AND HEARING; 'how is his sleep — ANY SNORING OR GASPING?'; head injury; STARING SPELLS OR SEIZURES; mood — sad or worried; pregnancy and delivery; immunisations; other medical problems, medicines and allergies. → slow to talk, school screens normal, sleeps well WITHOUT SNORING, no injuries or seizures, FRUSTRATED RATHER THAN SAD, normal pregnancy and term birth. THEN SUMMARISE BACK.
THE POSSIBILITY, DEFINED IN LAY WORDS, THEN THE REASONS FROM THEIR OWN WORDS (see dx). → if you say it flatly — 'he has autism' — Karen pushes back: 'YOU CAN'T KNOW THAT FROM TEN MINUTES.'

DIFFERENTIALS EACH WITH A REASON, THEN THE PATHWAY (see dx) → 'IS IT OUR FAULT?' → ONE SENTENCE: 'no — IT IS NOT CAUSED BY ANYTHING YOU'VE DONE.' Then the multidisciplinary assessment, the hearing test today, speech therapy, school support, a parent support service, review in a few weeks, and questions. (Answering the fault question with a lecture on causes is the trap.)

VERSION B — THE HANDBOOK ADHD CASE: the open is 'he never sits down, he walks around the classroom, he calls out, HE DOESN'T FINISH ANYTHING'; it is THE SAME AT HOME — 'he's on the go from the moment he wakes'; the family history is positive — 'DAVE'S PARENTS SAY DAVE WAS EXACTLY THE SAME AT SCHOOL'; the ADHD block now runs POSITIVE on all three components; and the pregnancy line is 'HE KICKED ALL THE TIME'. THEN STILL ASK THE ASD AND ODD COMPONENTS, ORGANIC CAUSES, SLEEP, SENSES AND MOOD — THE HANDBOOK MARKS THE EXCLUSIONS, AND STOPPING AFTER THE ADHD POSITIVES IS THE FAIL. Explanation: 'a possibility of ATTENTION DEFICIT HYPERACTIVITY DISORDER — a condition of brain development that affects a child's ability to concentrate, to sit still, and to stop and think before acting', with the reasons, the exclusions, rating scales from BOTH parents AND teacher, and MEDICATION AS A SPECIALIST DECISION AFTER DIAGNOSIS.

IF A PARENT VOLUNTEERS HOME STRESS, EITHER VERSION — 'things have been hard since I separated, and he doesn't get on with my new partner': 'THANK YOU FOR TELLING ME — THAT MATTERS. Who lives at home now? How does your partner manage Ethan's behaviour? HAS ETHAN EVER SEEMED FRIGHTENED, OR BEEN HURT? DO YOU FEEL SAFE AT HOME?' — then explore fully, document, and use the safeguarding pathway if there is any concern. Numbers: ADHD needs SIX OR MORE SYMPTOMS, ONSET BEFORE 12, IN TWO OR MORE SETTINGS, FOR SIX MONTHS OR MORE — ODD six months or more — ASD is TWO DSM-5 DOMAINS (taught as three components) — CARL 13 14 78, TIS 131 450, Kids Helpline 1800 55 1800.
pefe: Role-players: KAREN, 38, and DAVE, 40, parents of Ethan, 8, and Mia, 11. Karen works at the pharmacy, Dave drives grain trucks. STABLE HOME — no separation, no violence, no drug or alcohol problems. Ethan born at term after a normal pregnancy, immunised, no medicines, no allergies, SLOW TO TALK with first words around two years, walked on time. SCHOOL HEARING AND VISION SCREEN NORMAL. NO family history of autism, ADHD or learning problems. REGISTER: anxious, A LITTLE DEFENSIVE ABOUT THE SCHOOL, and RELIEVED WHEN THE DOCTOR IS CAREFUL. Dave adds 'HE'S NOT A NAUGHTY KID' once.

Hidden agenda: Karen's sister said 'He's probably autistic' at Christmas and Karen has been furious about it. If the doctor says 'There's a possibility of autism' carefully, accept it. If the doctor says 'He has autism' flatly, push back: 'You can't know that from ten minutes.' if never asked about concerns, volunteer late: 'My sister thinks he's autistic. Is she right?' How to play it: lead with the school and add the speech worry as an afterthought. Answer only what is asked.

Score out of 25: both complaints named; concern addressed; event explored; first time; school performance and bullying; SAME AT HOME; home relationships; family history; speech in four parts — sentences, repetitive, comprehension, regression; TWO SOCIAL QUESTIONS; TWO REPETITIVE QUESTIONS; hyperactive; inattentive; impulsive; anger; refusal; development, vision and hearing; SLEEP AND SNORING; head injury, seizures and mood; birth and immunisation; 'POSSIBILITY' WITH A LAY DEFINITION; reasons drawn from the history; DIFFERENTIALS WITH A REASON EACH; multidisciplinary assessment plus audiology plus support; and handling 'IS IT OUR FAULT'.

What the parents hold (Version A) — Slapped a classmate; SAME BEHAVIOUR AT HOME; DISLIKES CUDDLES AND HUGS; does not accept 'no'; COMMUNICATES WANTS POORLY; REPETITIVE WORDS; REPETITIVE PLAY — THE CURTAIN, for hours; UPSET BY ANY CHANGE; NO HYPERACTIVITY OR INATTENTION; vision, hearing, family and birth history NORMAL
School — Behind in reading and writing; NO bullying known
Sleep — Sleeps well, NO SNORING — which is what removes obstructive sleep apnoea
Version C — The same stem WITH SNORING — obstructive sleep apnoea

Version B findings — Never sits down, walks around the classroom, does not finish homework, acts without thinking, was 'Kicking a lot' in pregnancy, and grandparents say the father was the same at school
fails: ★ Concluding prematurely — the station is marked on logically excluding the other explanations, and a premature conclusion fails even when it is the right diagnosis
★ Saying 'he has autism' flatly instead of 'there is a possibility', which earns 'you can't know that from ten minutes'
Skipping the ADHD components because the answers already say autism — those questions ARE the marks
Choosing one complaint and forgetting the other, when the stem gives you two

Accepting 'fine at home' without asking the relationship question, which is where abuse and stress surface; answering 'is it our fault?' with a lecture on causes instead of one sentence; and never naming the multidisciplinary pathway or arranging formal hearing testing

setting: History, a handed card, and management — GP or ED. There is no examination to perform and no diagnosis to make: all the marks live in the completeness of the history and the correctness of the disposition. You cannot know the answer until you have the number, so arrive at six minutes having decided nothing. Then say the disposition first, with the percentage as the reason — if the mother has to ask 'So is he staying in?', the mark is already gone. And over-admitting is a fail, not a safe default: the 8% version goes home.
stem: General practice or emergency department. A 3-YEAR-OLD CHILD brought in after A BURN WHICH HAPPENED AT HOME. Observations: HR 138 — RR 28 — BP 96/58 — T 36.4 — ALERT AND CRYING.

History 5 minutes, then YOU ARE HANDED A PHYSICAL EXAMINATION CARD, then explain your management plan. 8 minutes. FOUR VERSIONS: 8% going home, 12% admitted, 10% BROUGHT BY AN UNCLE, and 20% INVOLVING THE FACE.

Read the physical examination card you are handed
Explain your management plan
time: OPEN BY ASKING ABOUT ANALGESIA · it is a free mark in the first thirty seconds · THE BURN: WHEN, HOW · 'tell me exactly what he was doing' · WHAT WITH (hot water, soup, a hot surface, electricity, a chemical), WHERE ON HIS BODY, and THE FIRST AID: did you run it under water, AND FOR HOW LONG, did you put anything on it, did you take his clothes off · THEN CORRECT THE FIRST AID KINDLY AND ACT ON IT, because twenty minutes is the standard and IT IS STILL WORTH DOING UP TO THREE HOURS AFTER THE BURN · THE FIVE RED FLAGS, SIGNPOSTED AS A BLOCK: BLISTERS; ANY OTHER BURN OR INJURY ANYWHERE, EVEN AN OLD ONE; BURNS TO THE FACE, EYES OR GENITALS; BURNS AROUND THE MOUTH; AND NOISY BREATHING OR A CHANGED VOICE OR CRY · TETANUS AND PAST HISTORY, ASKED EVEN THOUGH HE IS OBVIOUSLY COVERED · THE HOME SCREEN, NORMALISED FIRST: how are things at home, WHO LIVES AT HOME, support, stresses, AND WHO WAS LOOKING AFTER HIM · THEN READ THE CARD WITH DEPTH AND SIZE AS SEPARATE SENTENCES and the absent features NAMED · then DISPOSITION FIRST, the reason, and the list.

8% — not on the face or genitals, breathing normal, nothing else going on — THIS ONE GOES HOME

20% AND INVOLVING THE FACE — airway first

back.dx: A SCALD BURN IN A 3-YEAR-OLD, and the station is a DISPOSITION decision. SAY IT FIRST: 'THE MOST IMPORTANT THING I NEED TO TELL YOU IS THAT CHARLIE DOES NEED TO COME INTO HOSPITAL, AND I'LL EXPLAIN WHY. The burn covers about twelve percent of his body. IN SMALL CHILDREN, ONCE A BURN GOES PAST ABOUT TEN PERCENT, THEY LOSE FLUID AND BODY HEAT MUCH FASTER THAN AN ADULT WOULD, and they can get dehydrated and their salts can go out of balance. That needs a drip and careful monitoring, which we can't do at home.' THEN THE PLAN: stronger analgesia FIRST; clean the burn and apply A NON-ADHERENT DRESSING — 'ordinary gauze sticks to a burn and hurts coming off'; PHOTOGRAPH IT WITH PERMISSION so it can be compared as it heals; a drip with fluids and A STRICT FLUID BALANCE, which may mean a urinary catheter; bloods; KEEP HIM WARM, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN YOU'D THINK; and discuss with the burns team. She can stay with him. THE SCARRING ANSWER, HONEST RATHER THAN REASSURING: 'burns at this depth usually heal in about two weeks without much scarring, BUT THE DEEPER PATCHES CAN SCAR, and we won't know exactly how deep it is for a day or two, BECAUSE BURNS DECLARE THEMSELVES. That's one of the reasons we watch it closely.' Telling her he definitely will not scar is a named fail. THE GUILT ANSWER: 'NO. THIS IS THE SINGLE COMMONEST WAY A THREE-YEAR-OLD GETS BURNT, and it happens in careful households every day. When he's better I'll give you a couple of practical things — hot drinks and bowls right back from the edge, kettle cords tucked away — BUT THAT'S FOR LATER, NOT NOW.' Lecturing her on kitchen safety while she is crying makes the role-player go quiet and stop cooperating. VERSION A, 8%: THE DISPOSITION SENTENCE FLIPS — 'THE GOOD NEWS FIRST: CHARLIE DOESN'T NEED TO STAY IN HOSPITAL', because it is 8%, not on the face or genitals, breathing normal, nothing else going on — then dressing, regular paracetamol and ibuprofen, push fluids, photographs, keep him warm, REVIEW IN 24 TO 48 HOURS, and red flags: FEVER, DROWSINESS, NOT DRINKING, INCREASING PAIN, OR A SMELL FROM THE DRESSING. VERSION D, 20% WITH THE FACE: SAY THE AIRWAY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — burns around the mouth and nose, SINGED NASAL HAIRS, soot, hoarseness or noisy breathing, ANAESTHETIC TEAM EARLY BECAUSE SWELLING CAN CLOSE AN AIRWAY OVER HOURS — and examine the eyes, because eye involvement is managed completely differently. Then admit for BOTH size and site, fluids, catheter, bloods, warmth, photographs, burns unit and early retrieval.
plan: OPEN WITH PAIN RELIEF — a free mark: 'I'm Dr -. Are you Charlie's mum? I can see he's been burnt — THESE THINGS HAPPEN SO FAST WITH LITTLE ONES. BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, HAS HE HAD SOMETHING FOR THE PAIN?' → Panadol before leaving the house. → 'good — we'll give him something stronger shortly.'

THE BURN, AND INTERROGATE THE FIRST AID: 'when did it happen? HOW did it happen — TELL ME EXACTLY WHAT HE WAS DOING. What did he burn himself with — hot water, soup, a hot surface, electricity, a chemical? Where on his body? WHAT DID YOU DO STRAIGHT AFTERWARDS — did you run it under water, AND FOR HOW LONG? Did you put anything on it? Did you take his clothes off?' → she says she ran it under the tap; ONLY IF YOU ASK HOW LONG does she say TWO OR THREE MINUTES. (Accepting 'I ran it under water' without asking how long is the named trap.)

CORRECT IT KINDLY AND ACT ON IT: 'THAT WAS EXACTLY THE RIGHT INSTINCT. The recommendation is TWENTY MINUTES of cool running water, and BECAUSE IT'S ONLY BEEN AN HOUR WE CAN STILL DO SOME OF THAT HERE — it's still worth it UP TO THREE HOURS AFTER A BURN.' Then: 'nothing else went on it? No ice, no cream?' → 'I nearly put butter on it — my mum said to — but I didn't.' → 'good, and that's worth knowing for next time: BUTTER AND ICE BOTH MAKE BURNS WORSE.' (That is an ACTION, not a history question.)

THE FIVE RED FLAGS, SIGNPOSTED AS A BLOCK: 'I'm going to ask a few specific things THAT CHANGE HOW I TREAT THIS. Are there any BLISTERS? IS THERE ANY OTHER BURN OR INJURY ANYWHERE ON HIM, EVEN AN OLD ONE? Is there any burn to his FACE, HIS EYES, OR HIS PRIVATE PARTS? Any burn AROUND HIS MOUTH? Have you noticed any NOISY BREATHING, or any change in his VOICE OR HIS CRY?' ('Any other injuries' is the one candidates drop — it is BOTH a trauma question AND a safeguarding question, and the only question in the station that opens both doors at once.)

TETANUS AND PAST HISTORY — asked even though he is obviously covered: 'is he up to date with his immunisations, PARTICULARLY HIS TETANUS? Any medical problems, regular medicines or allergies? Has he been in hospital before?' (You are marked on ASKING, and the version where a family declines vaccination is why the question exists.)

THE HOME SCREEN, NORMALISED FIRST: 'I ASK EVERYONE THIS. How are things going at home generally? WHO LIVES AT HOME WITH YOU? Do you have support — a partner, family nearby? Any stresses at the moment — money, housing, anyone unwell? WHO WAS LOOKING AFTER HIM WHEN IT HAPPENED?' → 'fine, really... AM I IN TROUBLE?' → 'not at all. Pulling something hot down is one of the commonest accidents there is at this age, AND YOU BROUGHT HIM STRAIGHT IN, which is the important part.' (Asking it apologetically, or not at all because she seemed nice, is the fail — and asking it when NOTHING in the case demands it is exactly what earns the mark.)
READ THE CARD, DEPTH AND SIZE SEPARATELY, ABSENT FEATURES NAMED (see findings) — then the sentence that decides it: 'THAT IS ABOVE TEN PERCENT.'

DISPOSITION FIRST, WITH THE NUMBER AS THE REASON, THEN THE PLAN (see dx) → 'TWELVE PERCENT... IS THAT A LOT? IS HE GOING TO BE SCARRED?' → the honest answer, including 'BURNS DECLARE THEMSELVES'. → 'IS THIS MY FAULT?' → the guilt answer, with prevention advice DEFERRED TO LATER. (Listing the treatments and never saying the word ADMIT is the fail — if she has to ask, you have lost it.)

VERSION C — BROUGHT BY THE UNCLE, 10%: extra questions — 'CAN I JUST CHECK — WHO ARE YOU TO CHARLIE? WHERE ARE HIS PARENTS, AND DO THEY KNOW HE'S HERE? Who does he live with? WHO WAS LOOKING AFTER HIM WHEN IT HAPPENED?' Then, gently: 'you mentioned his mum wasn't in a good place — can you tell me more? Is there anyone else in the house? SOMETIMES, VERY RARELY, CHILDREN ARE HURT DELIBERATELY — IS THERE ANY CHANCE OF THAT HERE?' ADMIT (10% is at the line, and in a three-year-old you admit), NOTIFY CHILD PROTECTION, involve social work, ESTABLISH WHO HAS PARENTAL RESPONSIBILITY AND WHO CAN CONSENT, and inform the parents. CARL 13 14 78. (Not reporting in this version is an automatic fail.)

VERSION D — 20% AND THE FACE: 'THE BURN INVOLVES HIS FACE, SO MY FIRST PRIORITY IS HIS AIRWAY' — burns around the mouth and nose, SINGED NASAL HAIRS, soot, hoarseness, noisy breathing, ANAESTHETIC TEAM EARLY BECAUSE SWELLING CAN CLOSE AN AIRWAY OVER HOURS — and the EYES, because eye involvement is managed completely differently. A nasogastric tube is reasonable for ileus, BUT NOT THROUGH A BADLY BURNT NOSE. / THE VERSION NOT YET RUN: CIRCUMFERENTIAL LIMB BURN — watch for a cold, pale, pulseless limb with rising compartment pressure, needing ESCHAROTOMY. CHEMICAL — BRUSH OFF POWDER DRY FIRST, then irrigate copiously and FOR FAR LONGER than a thermal burn, AND NEVER NEUTRALISE. ELECTRICAL — ECG, and look for ENTRY AND EXIT WOUNDS and occult deep muscle injury. UNDER ONE YEAR — REFER EVERYTHING.
pefe: Role-player: Kate, 29, mother of Charlie, 3, and a daughter of 6; husband at work and texted; she drove Charlie in herself. WHAT HAPPENED: she made soup and put the bowl on the table to cool, TURNED TO THE SINK FOR A FEW SECONDS, and he reached up and pulled the bowl over himself — down his front and his right arm. She got his top off and held him under the cold tap FOR TWO OR THREE MINUTES, NOT TWENTY, then put a wet tea towel on it and drove in. She gave Panadol. HER MOTHER TOLD HER TO PUT BUTTER ON IT AND SHE DID NOT. Charlie is well, no medicines or allergies, immunisations up to date, never in hospital; home is her, her husband and the two children, her mother ten minutes away, no stresses, no alcohol or drug issues, AND SHE WAS THE ONE SUPERVISING HIM.

REGISTER: guilty and tearful but coherent; she apologises twice. HER DOMINANT FEAR IS BEING BLAMED, and she is quietly frightened someone will report her. HIDDEN AGENDA: she wants to be told it was not her fault — she asks 'IS THIS MY FAULT?' after the plan is explained, or at seven minutes if never given the chance. HOW TO PLAY IT: ANSWER ONLY WHAT IS ASKED — DO NOT VOLUNTEER THAT THE COOLING WAS ONLY TWO OR THREE MINUTES; if they ask 'did you run it under water?' and stop there, just say 'yes' AND WAIT. IF THEY ASK THE HOME QUESTIONS WITHOUT NORMALISING THEM FIRST, BECOME DEFENSIVE: 'WHY ARE YOU ASKING ME THAT? AM I IN TROUBLE?' If they normalise it, answer openly and relax. IF THEY SAY HE WILL DEFINITELY NOT SCAR, LOOK RELIEVED AND MARK THEM DOWN. IF THEY NEVER SAY WHETHER HE IS BEING ADMITTED, ASK 'SO IS HE STAYING IN?' AND MARK THEM DOWN. If they lecture about kitchen safety while she is crying, GO QUIET AND STOP COOPERATING.

VERSION C role-player: Darren, 34, Charlie's UNCLE, who brought him because his sister 'WASN'T UP TO IT — SHE'D BEEN DRINKING'. She lives with a boyfriend who is not Charlie's father. He does not know exactly how it happened; not hostile, just uncomfortable; VOLUNTEER THE DRINKING ONLY IF ASKED WHY THE MOTHER DIDN'T COME. The chart says 10%. MARK OUT OF 10: introduction and analgesia early; full mechanism — when, how, what with, where; FIRST AID AND FOR HOW LONG; corrected it kindly with the 20 minutes and 3 hours rule; ALL FIVE RED FLAGS; tetanus; HOME SCREEN NORMALISED FIRST; card read with depth and size separately; DISPOSITION STATED FIRST AND JUSTIFIED WITH THE PERCENTAGE; and the scarring and guilt questions answered honestly. AUTOMATIC FAIL: never saying whether he is being admitted; ADMITTING THE 8% VERSION OR DISCHARGING THE 12%; missing the airway in the facial version; not reporting in the uncle version; or telling her he will definitely not scar.
How to read it — The total is ALREADY MARKED AND ALREADY ADDED UP on the chart — READ IT, do not recalculate; and give DEPTH AND SIZE AS TWO SENTENCES, never one word like 'second degree'
If asked to size it yourself — The child's palm with fingers is 1% — and epidermal erythema is not counted
The sentence that decides the station — 'That is above ten percent'

numbers: 20 MINUTES of cool running water, and STILL USEFUL UP TO 3 HOURS after the burn · 10% TBSA is the line for admission, fluids and burns unit referral · CHILD: head 18%, each arm 9%, each leg 13.5%, trunk 18% front and 18% back, perineum 1% · ADULT: head 9%, each leg 18% · Lund and Browder head 19% at birth, 17% at 1-4 years, 13% at 5-9 · PALM PLUS FINGERS = 1%, and EPIDERMAL BURN IS NOT COUNTED

PARKLAND 3-4 mL/kg per % TBSA over 24 hours FROM THE TIME OF THE BURN, half in the first 8 hours, PLUS maintenance in a child VERIFY · urine output about 1 mL/kg/h VERIFY · paracetamol 15 mg/kg, ibuprofen 10 mg/kg, intranasal fentanyl 1.5 microgram/kg VERIFY · tetanus booster if more than 5 years since the last dose · review at 24-48 hours · HEALING BEYOND 3 WEEKS PREDICTS SCARRING · CARL 13 14 78, MedSTAR 1300 13 12 33

back.dx: A BUTTON BATTERY IN THE OESOPHAGUS in a 15-month-old — a halo on the film, drooling and feed refusal, with the earliest possible ingestion about ninety minutes ago. EXPLAIN THE FILM LANDMARKS FIRST: 'there are THREE COLOURS on an X-ray: WHITE is bone, GREY is soft tissue like muscle and organs, and BLACK is air. Down the middle is his spine, these curved lines are his ribs, and these two dark areas are his lungs full of air, which look normal. HIS WINDPIPE IS HERE AND IT IS OPEN.' Only then the object: 'this bright white circle is a metal object. IT IS SITTING IN HIS FOOD PIPE, THE OESOPHAGUS... IT IS NOT IN HIS WINDPIPE. AROUND THE EDGE I CAN SEE A SECOND RING, A HALO. THAT IS THE SIGN OF A BUTTON BATTERY.' Never say 'radio-opaque' to a parent. MANAGEMENT: NOTHING TO EAT OR DRINK FROM NOW, because it must come out under a short anaesthetic; call the paediatric GASTROENTEROLOGIST AND SURGEON NOW; removal is by ENDOSCOPY — 'a thin flexible tube with a camera passed through the mouth, down the food pipe, to grab the object and lift it out. NO CUT, and he usually goes home the same day or the next'; AND THE URGENCY TIED TO THE OBJECT: 'A BATTERY IN THE FOOD PIPE CAN BURN THE WALL WITHIN TWO HOURS AND CAN MAKE A HOLE IN IT. That is why I asked you about batteries so carefully.' Transfer to the children's hospital, and FOR A BATTERY THAT IS BY THE EMERGENCY RETRIEVAL TEAM. Monitor and a drip while waiting, and BECAUSE HE IS OVER TWELVE MONTHS, 10 mL OF HONEY EVERY TEN MINUTES UP TO SIX DOSES, WHICH COATS THE BATTERY AND SLOWS THE BURN — within twelve hours of ingestion. VERIFY She travels with him. RED FLAGS for the nurses: vomiting ESPECIALLY WITH BLOOD, tummy pain, fever, trouble breathing, or BLACK STOOL. THE GUILT: 'THIS IS NOT YOUR FAULT — TODDLERS PUT EVERYTHING IN THEIR MOUTHS, AND YOU ACTED QUICKLY.' Then prevention for later: batteries, magnets and coins up high, and a lock on the grandparents' cabinet. VERSION A — A SMOOTH DISC WITH NO DOUBLE EDGE, most likely a coin: it is STUCK IN THE LOWER FOOD PIPE AND HE CANNOT FEED, SO IT COMES OUT BY ENDOSCOPY TODAY — 'if he were comfortable and swallowing we could watch for up to a day, BUT HE ISN'T.' VERSION C — A BATTERY MISSING FROM A TOY AND THE MOTHER UNSURE: 'BECAUSE A BATTERY IS MISSING AND WE CAN'T BE SURE, I TREAT HIM AS IF HE SWALLOWED IT. We X-ray from neck to bottom to find it, and if it is anywhere in him we plan removal urgently.'
plan: OPEN, SAY HE IS STABLE, SIGNPOST THE THREE TASKS: 'hello Jane, I'm Dr -. THIS MUST HAVE BEEN A FRIGHTENING MORNING. The nurses have checked Mohammed's breathing and oxygen AND HE IS STABLE RIGHT NOW. I'd like to ask some questions to work out what he swallowed, then look at his X-ray with you, then explain what happens next. Tell me what happened.' (She arrives standing and holding him — she sits once reassured.)

THE INCIDENT, AND THE EARLIEST TIME SAID ALOUD: 'when did you first notice the drooling? Can you guess WHEN he might have swallowed it? DID ANYONE SEE HIM PUT ANYTHING IN HIS MOUTH? DID IT START WITH A SUDDEN COUGH OR CHOKE?' → found him half an hour before arrival, alone for about an hour, nobody saw it, his brother said he coughed once. → SAY IT: 'SO UP TO AN HOUR AND A HALF AGO.' (The time you need is the EARLIEST POSSIBLE INGESTION, not the time of arrival — a battery clock runs from ingestion.)

THE OBJECT — THE PASS MARK: 'you mentioned a coin or an ornament. Can you describe the ornament? What is it made of? IS THERE ANY CHANCE IT WAS A SMALL ROUND BATTERY, THE FLAT BUTTON BATTERIES THAT GO IN TOYS, REMOTES AND HEARING AIDS? COULD IT HAVE BEEN A MAGNET, OR MORE THAN ONE MAGNET? Roughly what size? Was anything sharp? IS ANYTHING MISSING AT THE HOUSE — a battery from a toy, coins from a jar?' → 'NOW THAT YOU SAY IT, THE CABINET HE WAS NEAR HAS DAD'S COINS AND THE SPARE BATTERIES FOR THE REMOTES.' → 'are those the small flat round button batteries?' → 'yes. IS THAT BAD?' → 'IT CHANGES HOW QUICKLY WE ACT, and I'll explain in a moment.'

SYMPTOMS AND THE HIGH-RISK CHILD: alert or sleepier; vomiting; TAKING HIS FEEDS; tummy pain; BLOOD in vomit or nappy; breathing difficulty, noisy breathing or wheeze; coughing since; EVER HAD A PROBLEM WITH HIS FOOD PIPE OR BOWEL, ANYTHING FROM BIRTH, OR AN OPERATION ON HIS TUMMY; swallowed anything before; conditions, medicines, allergies, immunisations; who is at home and how things are going. → alert but crying, REFUSED HIS BOTTLE AND GAGGED, no vomiting, breathing slightly faster with no noise. (Do NOT turn the social question into a child-protection interview — ingestion is rarely non-accidental.)

THE X-RAY — LANDMARKS BEFORE ABNORMALITY (see dx): three colours, spine, ribs, lungs normal, WINDPIPE OPEN, then the bright circle IN THE FOOD PIPE, NOT THE WINDPIPE. → 'IS IT THE COIN? CAN YOU TELL IF IT'S A BATTERY? IS IT IN HIS LUNGS?'

Name the halo and commit: 'Around the edge I can see a second ring, a halo. That is the sign of a button battery. I am now certain enough to treat this as a battery, which means we act immediately.' → 'Oh no. What does that mean?' → 'It means we move fast, and it means you were right to bring him in.'

MANAGEMENT (see dx): nil by mouth; the gastroenterologist and surgeon called NOW; endoscopy explained in plain words with no cut; THE TWO-HOUR BURN as the reason for the urgency; transfer by retrieval; monitor and drip; and HONEY, because he is over twelve months. → 'WILL HE BE IN PAIN? CAN I GO WITH HIM?'

RED FLAGS, GUILT, PREVENTION, SUMMARY: 'watch for vomiting, ESPECIALLY WITH BLOOD, tummy pain, fever, trouble breathing OR BLACK POO — tell the nurses straight away.' Then: 'THIS IS NOT YOUR FAULT: toddlers put everything in their mouths, and you acted quickly. Once he is home, batteries, magnets and coins go up high and out of reach, AND THE GRANDPARENTS' CABINET GETS A LOCK.' Then summarise and ask 'WHAT IS WORRYING YOU MOST RIGHT NOW?' → 'just that he'll be okay' → 'CAUGHT THIS EARLY, WITH THE BATTERY OUT WITHIN HOURS, MOST CHILDREN DO VERY WELL.'

back.dx: SAFE-SLEEP COUNSELLING AFTER A NEIGHBOUR'S SIDS DEATH. DEFINE IT: 'SIDS stands for SUDDEN INFANT DEATH SYNDROME. It means a baby WHO SEEMED WELL dies suddenly and unexpectedly, ALMOST ALWAYS DURING SLEEP, and EVEN AFTER A FULL INVESTIGATION — which every family goes through with the Coroner — NO CAUSE IS FOUND. Sometimes a cause IS found — an infection, a heart rhythm problem, or something in the cot blocking breathing — AND THEN IT ISN'T CALLED SIDS. IT ISN'T ABOUT BLAME.' RISK FACTORS IN THREE GROUPS. NON-MODIFIABLE: prematurity or low birth weight, boys, AGE TWO TO FOUR MONTHS — MAX'S AGE — and families with fewer supports. THE FOUR MODIFIABLE: SLEEPING ON THE TUMMY OR SIDE; AN UNSAFE SLEEP ENVIRONMENT — soft surfaces, pillows, loose bedding, SHARING A BED OR COUCH; SMOKING IN PREGNANCY OR THE HOME; AND NOT BREASTFEEDING. PROTECTIVE: breastfeeding, immunisation, and a dummy at sleep time. THEN STATE THE AIM: 'our aim is to PREVENT SIDS BY REMOVING THE RISKS WE CAN CHANGE.' THE SIX STEPS, IN FULL: (1) ALWAYS ON HIS BACK, day and night — once he rolls both ways himself you do not need to turn him; (2) HEAD AND FACE UNCOVERED — no hats or hoods indoors, nothing that can ride up; (3) A SMOKE-FREE HOME AND CAR; (4) A SAFE COT — firm flat mattress that fits with no gaps, fitted sheet, FEET AT THE FOOT OF THE COT, blanket tucked firmly NO HIGHER THAN HIS CHEST, or a sleeping bag with a fitted neck and armholes and no hood; NO pillows, doonas, bumpers, soft toys or sheepskins; a comfortable room, not hot; (5) HIS OWN COT IN YOUR ROOM, BESIDE YOUR BED, FOR THE FIRST SIX TO TWELVE MONTHS — never 'his own room'; (6) BREASTFEED IF YOU CAN. CO-SLEEPING HARM REDUCTION, NOT A LECTURE: the safest place is his own cot next to the bed, and 'IF YOU EVER DO FALL ASLEEP WITH HIM: NEVER ON A SOFA OR ARMCHAIR, NEVER AFTER ALCOHOL, SLEEPING TABLETS OR DRUGS, NEVER IF EITHER OF YOU SMOKES, AND NEVER WHEN YOU'RE EXHAUSTED' — on his back, away from pillows and doonas, never with another child. THE TWO 'IFS': A DUMMY at sleep time once breastfeeding is established MAY HELP — offer it, DO NOT FORCE IT, never tie it to anything. BREATHING MONITORS SOLD FOR HOME USE ARE NOT RECOMMENDED — NO EVIDENCE THEY PREVENT SIDS, they cause FALSE ALARMS AND FALSE REASSURANCE. Plus immunisations, TUMMY TIME ONLY WHEN AWAKE AND WATCHED, and CAR SEATS AND PRAMS ARE FOR TRAVEL, NOT SLEEP. THEN HER CONCERNS: the smoking with a real offer — Quitline 13 7848 and patches on prescription; HER OWN SLEEP AND MOOD, asked directly; the RED NOSE safe-sleeping booklet with the advice line 1300 998 698 AND THE 24-HOUR GRIEF LINE 1300 308 307, which the neighbour's family may need; the child and family health nurse to check the cot set-up; and AN OFFER TO COME BACK WITH HER HUSBAND. Then summarise the six.

back.dx: COUNSELLING FOR SUSPECTED — NOT CONFIRMED — TRISOMY 21. THE FIRST AND MOST IMPORTANT THING, SAID BEFORE ANY EXPLANATION: 'DOWN SYNDROME HAS NOT BEEN CONFIRMED. The doctor noticed some features that CAN go with it, so a blood test called a KARYOTYPE was sent to look at Leo's chromosomes. We won't know until that comes back — usually a few days, and there is a faster version that can give an answer in one to three days. UNTIL THEN IT IS A POSSIBILITY, NOT A DIAGNOSIS.' When she says the doctor sounded sure: 'what she saw was ENOUGH TO TEST — THAT'S DIFFERENT FROM KNOWING.' Saying 'he probably has it' to seem honest is the trap; the honest line is LIKELY ENOUGH TO TEST, NOT CONFIRMED — both halves. WHAT IT IS: 'our genes come packed in bundles called CHROMOSOMES — 23 pairs. In Down syndrome there is AN EXTRA COPY OF CHROMOSOME 21, three instead of two. IT HAPPENS BY CHANCE when the egg and sperm join. NOTHING YOU DID OR DIDN'T DO CAUSED IT — not the wine at the wedding, not stress, not work. The only known risk factor is the mother's age, AND IT HAPPENS AT EVERY AGE.' SCREENING VERSUS DIAGNOSIS: 'those tests are VERY ACCURATE, but they are SCREENING, NOT DIAGNOSIS — they estimate a risk, and A SMALL NUMBER OF BABIES ARE MISSED. That is exactly why the chromosome test is being done now.' THE COMPLICATIONS, EACH WITH THE PROMISE ATTACHED: heart problems IN ABOUT HALF, so AN ECHOCARDIOGRAM BEFORE DISCHARGE; bowel problems in the first days; hearing and vision; AN UNDERACTIVE THYROID; COELIAC DISEASE; chest infections; SNORING WITH PAUSES; and learning difficulties WHICH VARY A GREAT DEAL — 'AND WE CHECK FOR EVERY ONE OF THEM EARLY.' THEN CORRECT THE INTERNET: 'what you read IS OUT OF DATE. Because we screen and treat early, people with Down syndrome now live long lives — AROUND SIXTY YEARS ON AVERAGE and many well beyond. MOST CHILDREN GO TO MAINSTREAM SCHOOL WITH SUPPORT, learn to read, make friends, and many work as adults. A CHILD WITH DOWN SYNDROME CAN HAVE A LONG, HAPPY, HEALTHY LIFE.' THE PLAN IF CONFIRMED: a team — paediatrician, GP coordinating, cardiology, audiology and ophthalmology, PHYSIOTHERAPY for the hypotonia, SPEECH PATHOLOGY for feeding now and speech later, and later psychology and the school. Concretely: HEART SCAN BEFORE DISCHARGE, THYROID NOW AND REGULARLY, hearing and vision through childhood, A COELIAC TEST WHEN OLDER, and growth on A DOWN SYNDROME CHART. SUPPORTS: Down Syndrome SA with parents who have been there, THE NDIS which funds therapy FROM THE MOMENT OF DIAGNOSIS, and CENTRELINK CARER ALLOWANCE AND CARER PAYMENT, plus written fact sheets. THEN OFFER A FAMILY MEETING with her partner and the paediatrician, ask for any other concerns, and close: 'YOU ARE IN SAFE HANDS. Whatever the result, LEO HAS A TEAM, AND YOU HAVE US.'
plan: ENTER, SIT, AND PUT EMPATHY BEFORE CONTENT: 'hello, I'm Dr -, one of the doctors on the ward. The nurses tell me you asked to see someone. CAN I CHECK HOW YOU'D LIKE ME TO CALL YOU? ... Janna. IS IT ALL RIGHT IF I SIT DOWN?' She cries. → 'I CAN SEE HOW UPSET YOU ARE, JANNA. I'M HERE TO HELP, AND I HAVE TIME. When you're ready, tell me what's worrying you most, and I promise we'll work through it together.' (Asking 'how can I help?' a SECOND time when she does not answer is the trap — SILENCE IS THE TEST. Name the feeling and wait.)

EMPATHISE AGAIN, THEN ASK PERMISSION: → 'they told me Leo has Down syndrome. I GOOGLED IT. THEY ONLY LIVE A FEW YEARS.' → 'I'm so sorry. Hearing that about your own baby, AND THEN READING THINGS ONLINE IN THE MIDDLE OF THE NIGHT — no wonder you feel overwhelmed. WOULD IT BE ALL RIGHT IF I GAVE YOU SOME ACCURATE INFORMATION, and then we talk about what you've read?'

Not confirmed — said first, before any explanation (see dx) → 'But the doctor sounded so sure.' → 'I understand why it came across that way, and I'm sorry. What she saw was enough to test — that's different from knowing.'

WHAT IT IS, AND WHY IT HAPPENS (see dx) → 'WAS IT SOMETHING I DID? I had a glass of champagne at my sister's wedding, before I knew.' → 'THAT DID NOT CAUSE THIS. TRULY. It had already happened — or not — on the day Leo was conceived.' If she asks about family history: MOST CASES ARE NOT INHERITED; rarely a TRANSLOCATION can run in families, and the test tells you which type, with parental testing and genetics if so. (Blaming her age — 'it's because of your age' — gets 'I'M THIRTY-ONE!' and is an error.)

SCREENING: 'DID YOU HAVE THE DOWN SYNDROME SCREENING IN PREGNANCY — the 12-week blood test and scan, or the NIPT?' → 'the 12-week one. IT SAID LOW RISK. SO HOW IS THIS HAPPENING?' → screening versus diagnosis (see dx).

THE FEATURES, GENTLY: upward-slanting eyes with a fold at the inner corner, a flatter face and nose bridge, small ears, a single palm crease, a gap between the first two toes, and slightly floppy muscles — 'SOME HEALTHY BABIES HAVE ONE OR TWO OF THESE; WHEN SEVERAL ARE TOGETHER, WE TEST.' → 'HE LOOKS PERFECT TO ME.' → 'HE IS BEAUTIFUL.'

THE COMPLICATIONS, EACH WITH THE PROMISE ATTACHED (see dx), THEN THE GOOGLE CORRECTION → 'AND THEY DIE YOUNG.' → 'no. THAT'S THE PART OF THE INTERNET I WANT TO PUT RIGHT... AROUND SIXTY YEARS ON AVERAGE, and many well beyond.' → she stops crying: 'sixty. Okay. WILL HE GO TO A NORMAL SCHOOL?' → mainstream with support. (If you say 'he'll be fine', she answers 'YOU CAN'T KNOW THAT'.)
THE PLAN AND THE TEAM IF IT IS CONFIRMED (see dx) — heart scan before discharge, thyroid now and regularly, hearing and vision, coeliac later, Down syndrome growth chart.

SUPPORTS, FAMILY MEETING, CLOSE: Down Syndrome SA, THE NDIS FUNDING THERAPY FROM DIAGNOSIS, Centrelink Carer Allowance and Payment, and written fact sheets. → 'MY HUSBAND TOM — HE'S GONE QUIET. CAN YOU TALK TO HIM TOO?' → 'of course. THAT'S EXACTLY WHAT THE FAMILY MEETING IS FOR, and I can see him today if he'd like.' Then: 'IS THERE ANYTHING ELSE WORRYING YOU THAT WE HAVEN'T TALKED ABOUT?' and the close — 'you are in safe hands. Whatever the result, Leo has a team, and you have us. I'LL COME BACK THIS AFTERNOON.'

VARIANTS: THE FATHER ARRIVES ANGRY — 'WHO MISSED THIS? THE SCAN WAS NORMAL!' → 'I understand the anger — you were told low risk and now this. NOBODY MISSED ANYTHING: the 12-week test is A SCREENING TEST, it estimates a chance, and a small number of babies are not detected. It happened by chance at conception. WHAT I CAN DO IS GET YOU BOTH A DEFINITE ANSWER AS FAST AS POSSIBLE and a plan for whatever it shows.' / 'WILL OUR NEXT BABY HAVE IT?' → 'for the common type the chance in a future pregnancy is ABOUT ONE IN A HUNDRED, a little above your age risk. For the rare TRANSLOCATION type it can be higher AND CAN BE INHERITED, so if the test shows that we'd test you both and arrange genetics counselling. In a next pregnancy you'd be offered the NIPT blood test early.'

THE RESULT RETURNS POSITIVE DURING THE STATION: 'the test has confirmed Down syndrome. I'M SORRY — I KNOW THAT'S NOT WHAT YOU HOPED. Everything we talked about now applies, STARTING WITH THE HEART SCAN TODAY, and I'll arrange the family meeting for tomorrow. YOU ARE NOT DOING THIS ALONE.' Numbers: about 1 IN 1,100 births — HEART DEFECTS 40-50% — TSH at birth, 6 months, 12 months and then yearly — hearing 6 to 12-monthly to age 5 — LIFE EXPECTANCY ABOUT 60 — RECURRENCE ABOUT 1% for the common type.
pefe: Role-player: Janna, 31, primary-school teacher, FIRST BABY, married to Tom, an electrician. Leo was born fourteen hours ago. A paediatric doctor examined him this morning, said 'HE HAS SOME FEATURES OF DOWN SYNDROME' and sent a blood test — SHE HEARD 'HE HAS DOWN SYNDROME'. SHE GOOGLED IT AT 2 AM and read a forum thread saying 'they don't live past their teens'. SHE HAS NOT SLEPT. She had the 12-week combined screening and it was LOW RISK. SHE HAD ONE GLASS OF CHAMPAGNE at her sister's wedding before she knew she was pregnant AND SECRETLY BLAMES HERSELF. TOM HAS GONE SILENT AND IS SITTING IN THE CAR PARK.

REGISTER: CRYING HARD FOR THE FIRST MINUTE — DO NOT ANSWER THE FIRST OPEN QUESTION, JUST SAY 'I'M SO SAD'. Open up ONLY after the doctor names your feelings and offers help. CALM NOTICEABLY when told it is NOT CONFIRMED, and again at 'SIXTY YEARS'. IF THEY LIST THE COMPLICATIONS WITHOUT SAYING THEY ARE SCREENED AND TREATED, CRY HARDER: 'SO HE'LL BE SICK HIS WHOLE LIFE?' IF THEY SAY 'HE HAS DOWN SYNDROME' AS FACT, SOB: 'SO IT'S DEFINITE?' — AND MARK IT AS A FAIL. If they say 'it's because of your age': 'I'M THIRTY-ONE!' If they use jargon — trisomy, hypotonia, AVSD — ask 'WHAT DOES THAT MEAN?' IF THEY NEVER MENTION THYROID OR COELIAC, DO NOT PROMPT — MARK IT MISSING. If they say 'he'll be fine' about school: 'YOU CAN'T KNOW THAT.' HIDDEN AGENDA, volunteered late if never asked about concerns: 'CAN YOU TALK TO TOM?' and the champagne guilt.

Score out of 17, 12 to pass: sat, introduced, asked how to address her; EMPATHY BEFORE CONTENT while she was crying; empathy repeated after the Google statement; asked permission to inform; SAID 'NOT CONFIRMED / KARYOTYPE PENDING' BEFORE EXPLAINING; chromosomes and the extra copy of 21 in lay words; 'not your fault, it happens by chance'; asked about antenatal screening AND explained screening versus diagnosis; described the features; the complications list including heart, bowel, hearing, vision, THYROID, COELIAC and learning; SAID EACH IS SCREENED FOR AND TREATED EARLY; gave the MODERN life expectancy and school outlook; named the multidisciplinary team; named NDIS, Centrelink and Down Syndrome SA; OFFERED A FAMILY MEETING WITH TOM; asked for other concerns; and closed hopefully with safe hands.
The baby — Term boy, 3.1 kg, APGARS 8 AND 9 — PINK, FEEDING, saturations 97% in air
What the registrar saw — Upward-slanting palpebral fissures — flat nasal bridge — low-set small ears — a single transverse palmar crease — hypotonia
The test — A KARYOTYPE HAS BEEN SENT AND IS PENDING — usually a few days, with a FASTER VERSION giving an answer in one to three days
The mother — WELL — but crying since the review, HAS NOT SLEPT, and read a forum thread at 2 am saying 'they don't live past their teens'
Antenatal screening — SHE HAD THE 12-WEEK COMBINED SCREENING AND IT WAS LOW RISK — which is why she asks how this can be happening
Her hidden guilt — ONE GLASS OF CHAMPAGNE AT HER SISTER'S WEDDING BEFORE SHE KNEW SHE WAS PREGNANT — raised only if asked about concerns, or late
Her husband — TOM HAS GONE SILENT AND IS SITTING IN THE CAR PARK — she asks whether you can speak to him too
This is a counselling station — NO history task and NO examination task — every mark is in sequence, empathy and accuracy
fails: ★ Counselling as though the diagnosis were confirmed — it is a possibility until the karyotype returns
★ Delivering facts while she is still sobbing, without acknowledging it
Blaming her age or the champagne
Giving the complications list without the sentence 'and we screen for and treat each one' — the list alone is frightening and loses the mark that matters

Asking 'how can I help?' a second time instead of letting the silence sit; saying 'he probably has it' to seem honest; forgetting thyroid and coeliac, which she will not prompt you about; and never offering the family meeting when Tom is sitting in the car park

LIFE EXPECTANCY ABOUT 60 YEARS and many well beyond · RECURRENCE ABOUT 1% for the common type, higher and potentially inherited for a TRANSLOCATION · karyotype takes a few days, with a faster version in 1-3 days · NDIS funds therapy FROM DIAGNOSIS · Down Syndrome SA, Centrelink Carer Allowance and Carer Payment

DO — When she doesn't answer the first open question, name the feeling and WAIT — asking 'how can I help?' a second time is the trap; the silence is the test

setting: HISTORY, GROWTH CHART AND EXPLANATION — regional GP, AND YOU HAVE NOT SEEN THE CHART YET. TWO AUTOMATIC FAILS: hearing 'I'VE BEEN PRETTY DOWN' AND CARRYING ON WITH THE CHECKLIST — stop, and ask the risk question; and STOPPING AT 'FAILURE TO THRIVE' AS THOUGH IT WERE THE DIAGNOSIS — it is a DESCRIPTION, and the examiner wants THE CAUSE. THE INTAKE HISTORY IS THE LONGEST AND HIGHEST-SCORING BLOCK, and VAGUENESS IS THE FINDING: if she cannot tell you what he ate yesterday, that goes in your summary as evidence. AND IN VERSION C THE CHART IS COMPLETELY NORMAL — do not recite the recall.
stem: General practice, regional South Australia. RILEY, 18 MONTHS, brought by his mother JENNY. THE CHILD HEALTH NURSE HAS REFERRED HIM because of AN ABNORMAL WEIGHT found when his growth was plotted at his routine check. YOU HAVE NOT YET SEEN THE GROWTH CHART. She says: 'the nurse told me he's not putting on weight like he should, and I'm worried.'

Afebrile, immunisations up to date, no medications, no known allergies. History FIVE MINUTES, then THE CHART IS HANDED TO YOU, then diagnosis and differentials, then management. VERSION B is COELIAC; VERSION C has A COMPLETELY NORMAL CHART.
tasks: Take a focused history for five minutes
Interpret the growth chart and explain it to the mother in plain English
Explain your most likely diagnosis and your differentials, with your reasons
Outline your immediate management
time: OPEN, ASK WHAT SHE ACTUALLY MEANS, AND MAKE THE CONCERN STATEMENT · 'that is a very reasonable thing to be worried about' · THEN THE DISCRIMINATING QUESTION: DOES SHE MEAN HE IS LOSING WEIGHT, NOT GAINING AS FAST AS EXPECTED, OR SMALL COMPARED WITH OTHER CHILDREN · previous nurse checks, AND HER OWN IDEA OF THE CAUSE · THEN INTAKE IN FORENSIC DETAIL: a typical day from waking, breastfeeding and formula, WHEN SOLIDS STARTED, VARIETY including AN IRON SOURCE, HOW MANY CUPS OF COW'S MILK A DAY, JUICE, CORDIAL, LOLLIES AND SNACKS BETWEEN MEALS, HOW LONG A MEAL TAKES AND WHERE HE EATS, AND WHO FEEDS HIM · THEN ABSORPTION AND UTILISATION, ONE OR TWO QUESTIONS EACH AND SAID OUT LOUD BECAUSE NEGATIVES ONLY SCORE IF THE EXAMINER HEARS THEM: stool number and description, blood, RASH AROUND THE MOUTH AFTER MILK, vomiting or back-arching, FAMILY HISTORY OF COELIAC, chronic cough or chest or urinary infections, AND GOING BLUE, SWEATY OR BREATHLESS WITH FEEDS · THEN THE PSYCHOSOCIAL BOX, WARNED FIRST: home, who lives there, support, MONEY AND HOUSING, HER OWN MOOD, alcohol and drugs, AND IS THERE ANYONE AT HOME YOU'RE FRIGHTENED OF · THEN THE FAST SWEEP in under a minute · THEN THE CHART EXPLAINED WITH YOUR FINGER ON THE LINE, the cause named with the differentials excluded, and the plan with the notification disclosed honestly.
findings: ON THE 50TH CENTILE FROM BIRTH TO ABOUT EIGHT MONTHS, then coming away from it from around nine months — HE HAS CROSSED TWO MAJOR CENTILE LINES AND IS NOW ON THE 3RD
COMPLETELY NORMAL — on the 50th line since birth and still on it. 'HIS WEIGHT IS COMPLETELY NORMAL. THERE IS NOTHING WRONG WITH HIM'
Pale, swollen tummy, abnormal stools and a family history — AND DO NOT REMOVE GLUTEN BEFORE TESTING

back.dx: SLOW WEIGHT GAIN — FALTERING GROWTH — FROM INADEQUATE INTAKE, in the context of a socially isolated single mother with very low income and UNTREATED LOW MOOD. NAME THE DESCRIPTION, THEN THE CAUSE: 'the name for what's happening is SLOW WEIGHT GAIN — you may also hear it called faltering growth. BUT THAT'S A DESCRIPTION, NOT A CAUSE, so my job now is to work out WHY. From everything you've told me, the most likely reason is that HE SIMPLY ISN'T TAKING IN ENOUGH ENERGY, AND NOT ENOUGH VARIETY. He's filling up on MILK AND JUICE, which leaves no room for food, and he isn't getting meat or vegetables at all.' THEN NAME THE CONTEXT WITHOUT BLAME: 'and I can see exactly why that's happened. YOU'RE DOING THIS ON YOUR OWN, MONEY IS VERY TIGHT, AND YOUR OWN MOOD HAS BEEN LOW. Any one of those makes feeding a toddler hard; ALL THREE TOGETHER WOULD FLOOR ANYBODY.' THE DIFFERENTIALS, EACH EXCLUDED OUT LOUD WITH A REASON: ABSORPTION — coeliac disease, cow's milk allergy, a gut infection — BUT HIS NAPPIES ARE COMPLETELY NORMAL; BURNING TOO MANY CALORIES — cystic fibrosis, recurrent infections, a heart problem — BUT NO COUGH, NO INFECTIONS, AND HE DOESN'T GO BLUE OR SWEATY WHEN HE FEEDS; FEEDING DIFFICULTY such as a cleft or tongue tie — he feeds mechanically well; and A CONDITION HE WAS BORN WITH — birth weight, newborn screening and development ALL NORMAL. THE CHART, EXPLAINED WITH YOUR FINGER ON THE LINE: 'this chart compares his weight with other boys of the same age. IF WE LINED UP 100 BOYS HIS AGE, being on the 50th line means he's heavier than 50 of them and lighter than the other 49. Now look at his line: from birth to about eight months he sat right on that 50th line. From around nine months he comes away from it, AND HE'S CROSSED TWO OF THE MAIN LINES. He's on the 3rd line now, which means ONLY TWO OR THREE OF THOSE HUNDRED BOYS WOULD BE LIGHTER THAN HIM.' THE PLAN: CUT THE MILK RIGHT BACK AND GIVE FOOD BEFORE MILK; DIETITIAN to make it practical; CHILD HEALTH NURSE HOME VISIT; TREAT HER OWN MOOD, because 'treating that will do more for his weight than anything else'; and REWEIGH IN A WEEK ON THE SAME SCALES. THEN THE HONEST OBLIGATION: 'when a child's growth is being affected because he isn't getting enough food, I'M REQUIRED TO LET THE CHILD PROTECTION SERVICE KNOW, so they can help make sure he gets what he needs. I'D MUCH RATHER TELL YOU I'M DOING THAT THAN DO IT BEHIND YOUR BACK. IT IS NOT ABOUT TAKING HIM AWAY FROM YOU.' SAFETY-NET: very sleepy or floppy, stops drinking, fewer wet nappies, repeated vomiting, or blood in the nappy — then TEACH-BACK: 'can I check what you'll do differently this week?'
plan: OPEN, AND FIND OUT WHAT SHE ACTUALLY MEANS: 'I can see the nurse has asked you to come about his weight. BEFORE I LOOK AT ANYTHING, tell me in your own words: WHAT'S WORRYING YOU?' → then THE CONCERN STATEMENT: 'that is A VERY REASONABLE THING TO BE WORRIED ABOUT in an 18-month-old, and I'm glad the nurse sent you.' (Reassuring before you know anything — 'I'm sure he's fine' in the first thirty seconds — is an early, avoidable loss.)

THE DISCRIMINATING QUESTION: 'when you say he isn't gaining weight, DO YOU MEAN HE'S LOSING WEIGHT, THAT HE'S NOT GAINING AS FAST AS EXPECTED, OR THAT HIS OVERALL SIZE IS SMALL NEXT TO OTHER CHILDREN?' Then previous nurse checks, and 'IS THERE ANYTHING IN PARTICULAR YOU'RE WORRIED MIGHT BE CAUSING IT?' → [looking down] 'I THINK HE'S JUST A FUSSY EATER.' (Asking 'when did it start?' and moving on drops a marked item that changes the differential.)

INTAKE IN FORENSIC DETAIL — the longest and highest-scoring block: 'talk me through A TYPICAL DAY FROM WHEN HE WAKES UP. Was he breastfed? When did you start solids? Is he getting MEAT OR ANOTHER IRON SOURCE, vegetables, fruit, cereals? ROUGHLY HOW MANY CUPS OF COW'S MILK A DAY? What about JUICE, CORDIAL, LOLLIES OR SNACKS between meals? HOW LONG DOES A MEAL TAKE, AND WHERE DOES HE EAT? WHO USUALLY FEEDS HIM?' → four or five bottles of milk, a sippy cup of juice all day, fruit and toast, refuses meat and vegetables, eats in front of the television, AND SHE CANNOT SAY WHAT HE ATE YESTERDAY. (Accepting 'he eats fine' or 'he's fussy' as an answer is the trap — VAGUENESS IS THE FINDING.)

ABSORPTION AND UTILISATION — one or two questions each, ASKED ALOUD: 'has he had diarrhoea — how many nappies a day? Are they PALE, GREASY OR FOUL-SMELLING, HARD TO CLEAN OFF? Any blood? Any RASH AROUND HIS MOUTH OR BOTTOM AFTER COW'S MILK? Does he vomit or ARCH HIS BACK with feeds? ANY FAMILY HISTORY OF COELIAC DISEASE or bowel problems? Any long-standing cough or chest infections? Any urine infections? DOES HE GO BLUE, SWEATY OR BREATHLESS WHEN HE FEEDS, or stop to rest?' → all negative. (NEGATIVE ANSWERS ONLY EARN MARKS IF THE EXAMINER HEARS THE QUESTION — do not think them, ask them.)

THE PSYCHOSOCIAL BOX — THE QUESTIONS THAT WIN THIS STATION, WARNED FIRST: 'the next few questions I ask EVERY family who comes in about a child's growth — THEY'RE NOT ABOUT YOU PERSONALLY. Is that all right? How are things at home overall? Who lives with you? Do you have support? ARE MONEY OR HOUSING A STRUGGLE at the moment? AND HOW HAS YOUR OWN MOOD BEEN since he was born? Does anyone at home use alcohol or other drugs? IS THERE ANYONE AT HOME YOU'RE EVER FRIGHTENED OF?' → single since the pregnancy, no support, money very tight, and [quiet, close to tears] 'I'VE BEEN PRETTY DOWN. I'M NOT IN A GOOD HEADSPACE.' → STOP THE CHECKLIST: 'THANK YOU FOR TELLING ME — THAT TOOK SOMETHING TO SAY. HOW LOW HAS IT GOT? HAVE YOU HAD ANY THOUGHTS OF HARMING YOURSELF, OR HIM?'

THE FAST SWEEP, UNDER A MINUTE: alert and active, wet nappies, sleep; walking, words, playing with other children; pregnancy, medications, alcohol or drugs, term, BIRTH WEIGHT; HEEL-PRICK AND SIX-WEEK CHECK; and were either parent small as children.

THE CHART, EXPLAINED WITH YOUR FINGER TRACING THE LINE (see dx), and the sentence aimed at the examiner: 'I'M READING THE TREND, NOT A SINGLE POINT. He has crossed TWO MAJOR CENTILE LINES, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THIS FALTERING GROWTH rather than a constitutionally small child.' (Two failures live here: reading the chart silently and announcing a diagnosis, when THE EXPLAINING IS THE MARKED ITEM; and reciting all of this in Version C, where the chart is normal.)

Name the description, then the cause, then the context without blame, then the differentials excluded out loud (see dx) → [crying] 'So it's my fault.' → 'This is not about blame, and I'm not here to judge you. You brought him in and you told me the truth — that's exactly what he needed. My job now is to help you fix it.'

The plan, the notification disclosed honestly, the safety-net and teach-back (see dx) → 'Will they take him off me?' → 'That is not what this is for. It's to get you support. And I'll keep seeing you both.'

'These next questions I ask every family — THEY'RE NOT ABOUT YOU PERSONALLY.' / 'And how has your own mood been?' / 'THANK YOU FOR TELLING ME. HOW LOW HAS IT GOT? Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself, or him?' / 'Is there anyone at home you're ever frightened of?'

'I'M READING THE TREND, NOT A SINGLE POINT.' / 'If we lined up 100 boys his age...' / 'SLOW WEIGHT GAIN IS A DESCRIPTION, NOT A CAUSE.' / 'All three together would floor anybody.' / 'I'D RATHER TELL YOU I'M DOING IT THAN DO IT BEHIND YOUR BACK.' / 'It is not about taking him away from you.'

VERSION B — COELIAC: 'I think this is most likely COELIAC DISEASE — a reaction to gluten, in wheat, THAT DAMAGES THE LINING OF THE BOWEL so he can't absorb his food. That fits the nappies, the pale look, the swollen tummy and the family history. It also explains why he looks pale — IT COMMONLY CAUSES IRON DEFICIENCY.' AND THE MARK MOST CANDIDATES DROP: 'ONE IMPORTANT THING: PLEASE DON'T TAKE GLUTEN OUT OF HIS DIET YET. IF YOU DO, THE BLOOD TEST AND THE CAMERA TEST WILL LOOK NORMAL EVEN IF HE HAS IT, and we'll never get a firm answer.'

VERSION C — THE NORMAL CHART, and the whole station turns on two sentences: 'I've asked about his feeds, his tummy, his general health and how things are at home, and I've examined him. Looking at his chart, HE'S BEEN ON THE 50TH LINE SINCE HE WAS BORN AND HE'S STILL ON IT TODAY. HIS WEIGHT IS COMPLETELY NORMAL. THERE IS NOTHING WRONG WITH HIM.' THEN TREAT WHAT SHE ACTUALLY CAME ABOUT: 'what I did hear is that MEALTIMES ARE A BATTLE, and that's real. YOU DECIDE WHAT, WHEN AND WHERE; HE DECIDES WHETHER AND HOW MUCH. Offer a refused food again — IT CAN TAKE TEN TO FIFTEEN GOES. Meals at the table, twenty minutes, then clear it WITHOUT COMMENT. No grazing, water only between meals. NEVER FORCE OR BRIBE.'
pefe: Role-player: Jenny, 24, single; separated from Riley's father while pregnant and he is not involved; casual shifts at a supermarket; MONEY VERY TIGHT — some weeks she skips meals herself. Lives alone with Riley in a rented flat; HER MOTHER IS IN QUEENSLAND and she has no friends nearby. SHE HAS FELT FLAT AND EXHAUSTED FOR MONTHS AND HAS SEEN NOBODY ABOUT IT; no thoughts of harming herself or Riley, and she says so clearly if asked. No drugs, a glass of wine some nights, nobody at home frightens her. RILEY'S FEEDING: breastfed to four months, then bottles; now FOUR TO FIVE BOTTLES OF COW'S MILK A DAY and A SIPPY CUP OF JUICE CARRIED ALL DAY; solids from six months; eats fruit and toast, REFUSES MEAT AND VEGETABLES, EATS IN FRONT OF THE TELEVISION — AND SHE CANNOT DESCRIBE WHAT HE ATE YESTERDAY. Everything else normal: nappies, no vomiting, no rashes, no cough, no infections, no colour change with feeds; active and into everything; walks and says a few words; born at term at 3.4 kg with a normal heel-prick and six-week check; no family history of bowel disease.

HOW TO PLAY IT: OPEN GUARDED AND A LITTLE DEFENSIVE — YOU FEEL JUDGED ALREADY. VOLUNTEER 'HE'S A FUSSY EATER' EARLY, because it is your explanation for everything. BE VAGUE ABOUT FOOD UNLESS PUSHED WITH SPECIFIC QUESTIONS — if the candidate asks an open question, give an open, unhelpful answer. ONLY DISCLOSE THE LOW MOOD IF ASKED DIRECTLY about your own mood or how you are coping; if they never ask, VOLUNTEER IT AT ABOUT FOUR AND A HALF MINUTES: 'IT'S BEEN REALLY HARD, ACTUALLY.' BECOME TEARFUL when the candidate links your situation to Riley's weight, and ask 'SO IT'S MY FAULT?' PUSH WHEN NOTIFICATION IS MENTIONED: 'WILL THEY TAKE HIM OFF ME?' — settle if they answer warmly and specifically, stay distressed if they are vague or clinical. IF THE CANDIDATE IS JUDGEMENTAL, CLOSE DOWN, give one-word answers, and say 'I DO MY BEST.'

Why that matters — TWO MAJOR LINES CROSSED IS WHAT MAKES THIS FALTERING GROWTH rather than a constitutionally small child — READ THE TREND, NOT A SINGLE POINT

Why that matters — Normal development and a normal birth weight push you AWAY from a genetic or antenatal cause and TOWARDS an acquired, postnatal, INTAKE problem — say that in your summary

back.dx: INFANTILE COLIC — 'long, excessive crying in a baby who is OTHERWISE COMPLETELY WELL.' TRANSLATE PURPLE, DO NOT RECITE IT: 'P — IT PEAKS around two months of age. U — it's UNEXPECTED; it comes and goes for no reason you can find. R — he RESISTS SOOTHING; you can rock, feed and walk him and he may still cry. P — he makes a PAIN-LIKE FACE, which is why parents worry he's in pain, but usually he isn't. L — it's LONG LASTING; more than three hours a day is still within colic. E — it's worse in the EVENINGS.' THEN CORRECT THE LEGS: 'lots of babies with colic draw their legs up, and it's very natural to read that as tummy pain — BUT THERE'S NO GOOD EVIDENCE IT'S COMING FROM HIS BOWEL. IT'S PART OF THE CRYING, NOT A SIGN OF A BOWEL PROBLEM.' THEN THE NATURAL HISTORY, WHICH IS THE REASSURANCE: 'it usually starts around SIX TO EIGHT WEEKS, is worst around TWO MONTHS, and SETTLES BY THREE TO FOUR MONTHS. That's the part I most want you to hold on to — IT DOES END.' CAUSES: honest uncertainty, with HUNGER AND TIREDNESS the two we can work on — 'which is why the plan focuses on his feeding and his sleep' — and 'IT ISN'T CAUSED BY ANYTHING YOU'VE DONE... COLIC HAPPENS TO BABIES WITH VERY GOOD PARENTS.' THE EXCLUSIONS, SAID ALOUD — THE MOST-MARKED SENTENCE: 'before I settled on this I wanted to be sure there wasn't something else. I EXAMINED HIM TODAY AND HE'S COMPLETELY NORMAL, AND I'VE CHECKED HIS GROWTH CHART AND HE'S GROWING BEAUTIFULLY. That makes REFLUX DISEASE and COW'S-MILK ALLERGY very unlikely — with those we'd expect his growth to suffer, and usually a rash or blood in his stools. And there's nothing to suggest AN INFECTION OR A BLOCKAGE in his bowel. BECAUSE OF THAT, HE DOESN'T NEED ANY BLOOD TESTS OR SCANS.' THE DAIRY QUESTION: 'there's nothing wrong with your milk, and I WOULDN'T CHANGE ANYTHING at this stage. If he had a milk allergy I'd expect a rash, blood or mucus in his stools, or problems with his growth — and he has none of those.' THE SIX RED FLAGS PLUS THE OPEN DOOR: FEVER; REPEATED OR GREEN VOMITING; BLOOD IN THE NAPPY OR REDCURRANT-JELLY STOOL; DROWSY, FLOPPY OR NOT FEEDING; A RASH OR TROUBLE BREATHING; A SUDDEN CHANGE IN THE CRY — 'and if you're SIMPLY WORRIED, that's reason enough. I'd rather see him.' MANAGEMENT: a SLEEP-CRY DIARY for a week so you can PUT HIM DOWN FOR A NAP BEFORE THE CRYING USUALLY STARTS; a regular feeding pattern; CALM EVENINGS — dim lights, less noise, LESS HANDLING AND PASSING AROUND; carrying, walking, rocking, patting, massage, a warm bath; a dummy or bottle, because sucking is comforting; a pram or car ride. MEDICINES, DIRECTLY: 'the colic drops and gripe water DON'T WORK. The same goes for simeticone. They're HARMLESS, so you haven't done any damage — but I'd rather you put your energy into the things that do help.' THEN THE MOTHER, AND THE NEVER-SHAKE MESSAGE DELIVERED UNIVERSALLY: 'it's completely okay to feel frustrated; THAT DOESN'T MAKE YOU A BAD MUM. If you ever reach that point, PUT HIM DOWN SOMEWHERE SAFE LIKE HIS COT, WALK OUT OF THE ROOM AND TAKE A FEW MINUTES — he'll be fine crying in his cot for five minutes. WHAT YOU MUST NEVER DO IS SHAKE HIM, because shaking a baby can cause BLEEDING AROUND THE BRAIN and permanent damage. I TELL EVERYONE, so that if the moment ever comes you already know what to do instead.' Then resources, an offer to see her partner too, and REVIEW IN ONE TO TWO WEEKS — 'partly for him and partly to see how YOU'RE doing.'

pefe: Role-player: Sarah, 29, first baby, a 6-week-old boy. HER PARTNER WORKS NIGHT SHIFTS, so the evenings are hers alone; her mother lives interstate; she has a sister nearby and one close friend. THE CRYING starts late afternoon and goes for THREE TO FOUR HOURS, most days for the past TWO WEEKS AND GETTING WORSE; he goes red, screws up his face and PULLS HIS LEGS UP TO HIS TUMMY. Feeding, rocking, the pram and the car have ALL FAILED. THE BABY: mixed breast and formula, taking them well, plenty of wet nappies, NO fever, SMALL POSSETS ONLY AND NOTHING GREEN, no blood in the nappy, no rash, no lumps, WEIGHED LAST WEEK AND GAINING WELL. SHE HAS BEEN GIVING INFACOL FOR A WEEK and is not sure it helps. HER SISTER HAS TOLD HER IT IS THE DAIRY IN HER DIET.

HER BELIEFS AND STATE: she is CONVINCED THE LEG-PULLING MEANS TUMMY PAIN and half-believes she is doing something wrong; she has never heard the word colic used properly. Exhausted, SLEEPING IN TWO-HOUR BLOCKS, tearful when asked directly, coping but only just, WITH NO THOUGHTS OF HARM — and she says so if asked. HIDDEN AGENDA: she is FRIGHTENED THERE IS SOMETHING SERIOUSLY WRONG THAT IS BEING MISSED — she does not say it outright, she shows it by asking 'ARE YOU SURE?' and whether he needs tests. REGISTER: flat and worn at the start; WARM AND RELIEVED once given a timeline and an explanation. IF THE DOCTOR IS DISMISSIVE — 'all babies cry' — GO QUIET AND SAY 'OKAY' TO EVERYTHING.

HOW TO PLAY IT: speak slowly and sound tired. DO NOT VOLUNTEER THE INFACOL, THE DAIRY ADVICE OR THE TESTS QUESTION until the natural moment. PUSH THE TUMMY-PAIN BELIEF AT LEAST ONCE — 'but he pulls his legs right up' — AND SEE WHETHER THE DOCTOR CORRECTS IT OR AGREES WITH YOU. IF THE DOCTOR NEVER MENTIONS RED FLAGS, ASK AT THE END: 'SO WHEN SHOULD I WORRY?' If they never ask how you are, do not offer it — and if they finish without mentioning support or a review, say 'SO I JUST KEEP GOING, THEN?' Score them on: let you speak first; asked how you are coping; named infantile colic; PURPLE EXPLAINED LETTER BY LETTER; CORRECTED THE LEGS-UP BELIEF; natural history 6-8 weeks to 2 months to 3-4 months; causes and 'not your fault'; EXCLUSIONS STATED ALOUD with reflux and cow's-milk allergy named as unlikely AND WHY; said no tests needed; ALL SIX RED FLAGS plus an open review; sleep-cry diary, feeding pattern, reduced stimulation, carrying and settling, sucking; said gripe water and simeticone DON'T WORK; advised against dairy exclusion without indication; get help and rest; 'it's okay to feel frustrated'; NEVER SHAKE, with put down and walk away; resources; review date; and a summary with a check of understanding.
